From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review (Buyer Perspective)

## Bottom line

The Seller's package is not acceptable as drafted. Taken together, its provisions would leave the Buyer with almost no warranty recourse for the problems the data room has already identified:

- **General data-room disclosure (1.1, 1.2)** fairly discloses everything in the data room.
- **Buyer-knowledge bar (8.3)** excludes any matter the Buyer knew of or could have found in the data room.
- **Deductible basket and per-claim de minimis (12.2)** absorb the first AUD 250,000 of claims.
- **Cap at 20%, or AUD 4.8m (12.1)** applies even to title and capacity.
- **18-month claims window (12.3)** applies to all claims.
- **Exclusive-remedy and non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5)** apply to all claims, including fundamental ones.

Layered together, these mean that a disclosed problem is effectively uninsured by the SPA. The Buyer should not try to fix known issues through warranty claims. It should fix them through price, conditions precedent (CPs), specific indemnities, retentions or escrow, and pre-Completion remediation.

Two framing points:

- **The "FINAL / not to be re-opened" label and the market-norms preamble** are negotiating pressure, not binding terms. Wattlebridge has not agreed these positions. The deal team should confirm whether any principal-level commitments were actually made, and benchmark the stated market ranges against its own precedent data rather than the Seller's characterisation. Note that the Seller's own cited ranges are at the seller-friendly end on cap (20%) and time (18 months).
- **The disclosure is stale.** Its data room cut-off is 5.00pm on 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so the Buyer needs a bring-down of the data room and disclosure before signing or Completion.

## Known exposures

| Item | Source | Amount / scale | Seller's position | Buyer risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bluefen change-control consent | DD-002, Disc. §2 | ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30% of FY26) | Reasonable endeavours; treated as satisfied on "delivery of written consent" | Loss of ~30% of revenue, plus conditions in cl. 11.3 unmet |
| Riverlark facility | DD-003, Disc. §3 | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding | Release "following Completion" | Debt left in the business; security may survive Completion |
| Ironquay SOW3 | DD-004, DD-010, Disc. §4 | AUD 180k open; IP transfer conditional on payment | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Unpaid fees; title to project materials not transferred |
| Employee bonuses | DD-005, Disc. §5 | AUD 420k (plus payroll tax, super, on-costs) | "A matter for the Seller"; not in funds flow | Cash leakage; costs excluded from the funds flow |
| Privacy incident | DD-006, Disc. §6 | ~1,240 records (names, emails, roles, timestamps) | "Preliminary", "not expected to be material" | Notification and regulatory costs, claims, remediation |
| Supplier renewals | DD-008, DD-011, Disc. §8 | AUD 330k aggregate | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Possibly unavoidable pre-Completion commitments |
| Office lease | DD-007, Disc. §7 | Unquantified | Notification obligation only | Possible landlord consent requirement |
| Mossvale | DD-009, Disc. §9 | Unquantified | Assignment restriction; consent not stated as needed | Possible consent requirement on share sale |

The quantified items total about AUD 4.1m, which is close to the Seller's 4.8m cap. Under the Seller's drafting, most of this would be unrecoverable.

## Issue-by-issue analysis and pushback

### 1. General disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7)
**Departure:** The Seller discloses every fact in the data room and in public registers. This is a blanket disclosure that overrides the warranties.
**Pushback:** Delete. Disclosure should be fair, fairly specific, and made against a specific warranty. Data-room documents should be disclosed only if specifically referred to, with a fair summary. Public searches should be limited to a named list. 1.4 (no admissions) is acceptable as drafted.

### 2. Buyer knowledge (8.3)
**Departure:** The Buyer loses claims for anything it knew, or could have discovered, from the data room or public records. This is the most damaging clause in the package because almost every known issue sits in the data room.
**Pushback:** Delete. Insert an express pro-sandbagging clause: the Buyer's rights are not affected by its knowledge or investigations. The position on knowledge-based claims in Australia is not settled, so an express clause matters. Known issues then go to specific indemnities and price, not warranties.

### 3. Caps (12.1) and fundamental warranties
**Departure:** A 20% cap (AUD 4.8m) applies to general claims. Title and capacity are capped at the same level, for "administrative simplicity".
**Pushback:**
- General warranties: negotiate a higher cap, targeting at least 30% or more depending on the deal team's valuation view and the warranty package.
- Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency): cap at 100% of the price, with a limitation period of at least six years, or the statutory period if longer.
- Tax: specific tax indemnity, not capped at the general cap, running until 60 days after the relevant assessment period expires, or as otherwise agreed with NSW counsel.
- Known-issue specific indemnities (below): separate cap, not counted against the general cap.

### 4. Thresholds (12.2)
**Departure:** A AUD 25,000 de minimis per claim and a AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable. The basket is a deductible, so the Buyer bears the first ~1% of price.
**Pushback:**
- Reduce the de minimis (AUD 5,000–10,000) and aggregate related claims arising from the same facts.
- Change the basket to a tipping basket: once exceeded, the Buyer recovers from the first dollar.
- Lower the basket where possible, and note that a deductible basket is especially harmful given the size of known exposures.

### 5. Time limits (12.3, 13)
**Departure:** 18 months for general warranties, and the same limit applies to all claims.
**Pushback:**
- General warranties: at least 24–36 months, given that a SaaS business's tax, privacy and IP exposures may only surface after the first audit or annual cycle.
- Fundamental warranties and tax: six years (the NSW statutory period for contract claims under the Limitation Act 1969 is generally six years), or the tax period.
- Known-issue indemnities: survival aligned with the underlying exposure (for example, IP or privacy claims may run longer).
- Resist any drafting that shortens the period below the statutory period without clear agreement.

### 6. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (9.3, 12.8, 20.5)
**Departure:** Apply to all claims of any nature.
**Pushback:** Carve out fraud expressly, and carve out fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustments, and any claim for specific performance or injunctive relief. Non-reliance should not limit the Buyer's rights in respect of fraud or the Seller's own statements in the SPA.

### 7. Bluefen (cl. 3, 6.3, Disc. §2)
**Departure:** The Seller will use "reasonable endeavours" and treat consent as satisfied once written consent is delivered, even if the conditions in cl. 11.3 are unmet.
**Pushback:**
- Make the Bluefen consent, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer and with all cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived by Bluefen in writing, an express CP.
- Seller to use all reasonable endeavours at its own cost, and to bear the cost of satisfying any conditions.
- Buyer termination right if the CP is not satisfied by a long-stop date.
- Consider a price adjustment, escrow or earn-out tied to Bluefen revenue retention for a defined period.
- Warranty that no Bluefen notice of termination, variation or dispute has been given.

### 8. Riverlark (cl. 2, 7, Disc. §3)
**Departure:** AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the security release comes "following Completion".
**Pushback:** This is inconsistent with a debt-free, cash-free deal. The Buyer should require:
- A payoff letter confirming the amount, with a deduction from the price at Completion.
- Repayment from the Seller's proceeds through the funds flow at Completion.
- Delivery at Completion of discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations and any guarantees), not after Completion.
- Confirmation whether the change-of-control provision in 8.1 is triggered, and a waiver if it is.

### 9. Ironquay IP (cl. 11.1, 4, Disc. §4)
**Departure:** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, and the Seller calls it "adequate". DD-010 shows AUD 180k open. No payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
**Pushback:**
- The Seller pays the AUD 180k before Completion, or it is deducted from the price or held in retention until paid.
- Delivery of a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 project materials as a CP.
- A broader IP ownership indemnity covering all Ironquay-developed materials, not just SOW3.
- Separate cap, longer survival, and no basket.

### 10. Employee bonuses (Disc. §5, funds flow)
**Departure:** AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses sit outside the funds flow, and the disclosure is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
**Pushback:**
- Treat all Completion bonuses, and related payroll tax, superannuation (currently 12% guarantee rate), and on-costs, as seller transaction costs or debt-like items deducted from the price.
- Require the funds flow to show them explicitly.
- Specific indemnity for all pre-Completion employee entitlements, bonuses and related taxes.
- Warranty on the complete list of employees and entitlements.

### 11. Privacy and export incident (cl. 4.6, Sch. 6, Disc. §6)
**Departure:** Described as preliminary and not expected to be material. The investigation is unfinished, and it is not known whether unauthorised access occurred, the scope, or whether notification is required.
**Pushback:**
- Before signing: obtain the forensic investigation outcome, a written assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) (which generally requires an assessment to be completed within 30 days of awareness), and the date the Company became aware of the incident.
- Specific indemnity for all losses arising from the incident, including regulatory costs, notification costs, remediation, claims and any OAIC action. Separate cap, not subject to the basket, survival at least six years.
- Warranty that no eligible data breach has occurred other than the disclosed incident.
- Seller to control the remediation at its cost, with Buyer consent over any notification or public statement affecting the Company.
- Consider an escrow or retention for the incident.

### 12. Office lease (cl. 7, Disc. §7)
**Departure:** Notification obligation only, with no statement on whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale.
**Pushback:** Obtain the lease and confirm whether the share sale is a change of control. If consent is required, make it a CP, with a landlord estoppel certificate.

### 13. Supplier renewals (Disc. §8)
**Departure:** Described as ordinary-course costs. The disclosure does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, or accrued.
**Pushback:** Require the contracts, and confirm whether any renewal commits the Company beyond Completion. Pre-Completion accrued costs and any unavoidable commitments outside the ordinary course should be deducted from the price, or treated as debt-like items. Warranty that no contract has been renewed or varied outside the ordinary course since the reference date.

### 14. Mossvale (Disc. §9)
**Departure:** An assignment restriction with no statement on whether consent is needed for the share sale.
**Pushback:** Obtain legal advice on the clause. If consent is required, make it a CP. Otherwise, obtain written confirmation from Mossvale.

### 15. Title (Disc. §10, DD-012)
**Departure:** The Seller relies on the share register (DD-012) showing Harbourglass as holder of 100% of the shares.
**Pushback:** The register is evidence, not proof. The Buyer should:
- Obtain a current ASIC company extract and an inspection of the original register, not a copy.
- Run PPSR and other encumbrance searches.
- Obtain warranties that the Seller is the sole legal and beneficial owner of 100% of the shares, free of encumbrances, with no options or rights to acquire any other shares.
- Make these fundamental warranties (see point 3).

### 16. Tax and IP ("settled under the general regime")
**Departure:** The Seller treats tax and IP warranties as covered by the general regime, which is capped and time-limited.
**Pushback:** Reject. Tax needs a standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity outside the general cap and basket. IP warranties need to cover title, non-infringement and open-source use, with longer survival.

## Recommendations (prioritised)

1. **Reject the general data-room disclosure (1.1, 1.2) and the buyer-knowledge bar (8.3).** Insert an express pro-sandbagging clause.
2. **Move known issues out of the warranty regime.** Use price adjustments, CPs, specific indemnities, retentions and escrow for Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy incident, supplier renewals, lease and Mossvale.
3. **Fix the Bluefen CP.** Full satisfaction of cl. 11.3 conditions, all reasonable endeavours at Seller's cost, and a termination right.
4. **Require Riverlark to be repaid and discharged at Completion** through the funds flow, not after it.
5. **Require the AUD 180k Ironquay payment and a confirmatory IP assignment** before Completion.
6. **Bring the AUD 420k bonuses and related payroll taxes and on-costs into the funds flow** as seller costs or debt-like items.
7. **Obtain the privacy incident investigation result before signing**, and add a specific indemnity with a separate cap and long survival.
8. **Reset the general warranty package:** a higher cap (at least 30%, to be set by the deal team), a tipping basket, a lower de minimis, and 24–36 months' survival.
9. **Fundamental and tax warranties:** cap at 100% of price, six years' survival (or the tax period), outside the general regime.
10. **Carve out fraud and specific indemnities** from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
11. **Verify title independently** (ASIC extract, original register inspection, PPSR searches), rather than relying on DD-012.
12. **Obtain a data-room bring-down** to the current date and update the disclosure accordingly.
13. **Confirm with the deal team** whether any principal-level commitments were made before this package was issued.

## Limits of this review

I have reviewed only the Seller's summaries and disclosure letter, not the full SPA, the underlying data-room documents, or the Buyer's valuation model. The statutory references (NSW Limitation Act 1969, Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) NDB scheme, superannuation guarantee rate) are general pointers and should be confirmed by NSW transaction counsel and, for privacy, by privacy counsel. The quantum of each exposure, and whether it should be handled through price or indemnity, depends on the deal team's valuation work, which I have not seen.

- Warranty on the complete list of employees and entitlements.

### 11. Privacy and export incident (cl. 4.6, Sch. 6, Disc. §6)
**Departure:** Described as preliminary and not expected to be material. The investigation is unfinished, and it is not known whether unauthorised access occurred, the scope, or whether notification is required.
**Pushback:**
- Before signing: obtain the forensic investigation outcome, a written assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) (which generally requires an assessment to be completed within 30 days of awareness), and the date the Company became aware of the incident.
- Specific indemnity for all losses arising from the incident, including regulatory costs, notification costs, remediation, claims and any OAIC action. Separate cap, not subject to the basket, survival at least six years.
- Warranty that no eligible data breach has occurred other than the disclosed incident.
- Seller to control the remediation at its cost, with Buyer consent over any notification or public statement affecting the Company.
- Consider an escrow or retention for the incident.

### 12. Office lease (cl. 7, Disc. §7)
**Departure:** Notification obligation only, with no statement on whether landlord consent is needed for the share sale.
**Pushback:** Obtain the lease and confirm whether the share sale is a change of control. If consent is required, make it a CP, with a landlord estoppel certificate.

### 13. Supplier renewals (Disc. §8)
**Departure:** Described as ordinary-course costs. The disclosure does not say whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable, or accrued.
**Pushback:** Require the contracts, and confirm whether any renewal commits the Company beyond Completion. Pre-Completion accrued costs and any unavoidable commitments outside the ordinary course should be deducted from the price, or treated as debt-like items. Warranty that no contract has been renewed or varied outside the ordinary course since the reference date.

### 14. Mossvale (Disc. §9)
**Departure:** An assignment restriction with no statement on whether consent is needed for the share sale.
**Pushback:** Obtain legal advice on the clause. If consent is required, make it a CP. Otherwise, obtain written confirmation from Mossvale.

### 15. Title (Disc. §10, DD-012)
**Departure:** The Seller relies on the share register (DD-012) showing Harbourglass as holder of 100% of the shares.
**Pushback:** The register is evidence, not proof. The Buyer should:
- Obtain a current ASIC company extract and an inspection of the original register, not a copy.
- Run PPSR and other encumbrance searches.
- Obtain warranties that the Seller is the sole legal and beneficial owner of 100% of the shares, free of encumbrances, with no options or rights to acquire any other shares.
- Make these fundamental warranties (see point 3).

### 16. Tax and IP ("settled under the general regime")
**Departure:** The Seller treats tax and IP warranties as covered by the general regime, which is capped and time-limited.
**Pushback:** Reject. Tax needs a standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity outside the general cap and basket. IP warranties need to cover title, non-infringement and open-source use, with longer survival.

## Recommendations (prioritised)

1. **Reject the general data-room disclosure (1.1, 1.2) and the buyer-knowledge bar (8.3).** Insert an express pro-sandbagging clause.
2. **Move known issues out of the warranty regime.** Use price adjustments, CPs, specific indemnities, retentions and escrow for Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy incident, supplier renewals, lease and Mossvale.
3. **Fix the Bluefen CP.** Full satisfaction of cl. 11.3 conditions, all reasonable endeavours at Seller's cost, and a termination right.
4. **Require Riverlark to be repaid and discharged at Completion** through the funds flow, not after it.
5. **Require the AUD 180k Ironquay payment and a confirmatory IP assignment** before Completion.
6. **Bring the AUD 420k bonuses and related payroll taxes and on-costs into the funds flow** as seller costs or debt-like items.
7. **Obtain the privacy incident investigation result before signing**, and add a specific indemnity with a separate cap and long survival.
8. **Reset the general warranty package:** a higher cap (at least 30%, to be set by the deal team), a tipping basket, a lower de minimis, and 24–36 months' survival.
9. **Fundamental and tax warranties:** cap at 100% of price, six years' survival (or the tax period), outside the general regime.
10. **Carve out fraud and specific indemnities** from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
11. **Verify title independently** (ASIC extract, original register inspection, PPSR searches), rather than relying on DD-012.
12. **Obtain a data-room bring-down** to the current date and update the disclosure accordingly.
13. **Confirm with the deal team** whether any principal-level commitments were made before this package was issued.

## Limits of this review

I have reviewed only the Seller's summaries and disclosure letter, not the full SPA, the underlying data-room documents, or the Buyer's valuation model. The statutory references (NSW Limitation Act 1969, Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) NDB scheme, superannuation guarantee rate) are general pointers and should be confirmed by NSW transaction counsel and, for privacy, by privacy counsel. The quantum of each exposure, and whether it should be handled through price or indemnity, depends on the deal team's valuation work, which I have not seen.
